clue.text: Extensive outdoor facility needed for a party

definitions.meaning: a site of tents or huts spread out in the open air
a faction or group holding shared views, as in the rival factions of a dispute

explanation.surface: A big outdoor site is required to host a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is both an open-air settlement of tents and a faction or side in a dispute.

clue.text: Luck finally out, has been sacked — should one 12 it?

indicators.note: something sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
the final letter of the word Luck is put out, leaving its first three

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose luck has run out has lost their job and wonders whether to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is SWALLOW, read here as eating rather than tolerating; 'finally out' drops the K, and 'sacked' scrambles the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a sticky currant pastry, something one might well eat.

clue.text: Press for an example of such communications

definitions.text: Press for an example of such communications

parts.words: Press for an example of such communications
parts.note: newspapers are one instance of the channels of mass communication, so the whole clue describes that plural group

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to give an instance of a kind of message.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is one example of the plural channels of mass communication, plural of medium.

clue.text: Taken by surprise, finding a few pounds, not the last I lost?

indicators.note: the final letter of the weight word is dropped

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds
taken as written
shed means lost, as a tree loses leaves

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find a little money, having lost something along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' suggests money but is weight: a STONE is 14 lb. Cut its last letter for STON, then add I and SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astonished is to be amazed, caught off guard by something unexpected.

clue.text: One-time reporter of racing results

parts.note: reads like a former turf journalist, but describes a device that reports times in races

explanation.surface: A retired journalist used to report the results of horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch measures and shows elapsed time, so it reports how long a race took.

clue.text: Plant manufactured old car — millions driven away

indicators.note: the letter for millions is removed from the carmaker's name

parts.note: Morris was a British carmaker whose models, like the Morris Minor, are now old cars

explanation.surface: A factory produced a vintage car, but the millions of profits have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: MORRIS was a British car manufacturer; 'Plant' looks like a factory but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is an iris whose fragrant root is used in perfumery, so it is a plant.

clue.text: One's tipped as having hidden depths

definitions.text: One's tipped as having hidden depths

parts.words: One's tipped as having hidden depths
parts.note: sounds like a person tipped for success with an inner life, but describes a floating mass with only its tip showing

explanation.surface: Someone is spoken of as having a deeper character than appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Only the tip of a floating ice mass shows above water, most of it lying hidden below.

clue.text: Try to organise a party

definitions.meaning: to attempt something, have a go
to throw a celebration, a bash being informal for a party

explanation.surface: Have a go at arranging a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech, having a bash is attempting something, and a bash is also a party.

clue.text: Rush to see Morse feature

definitions.meaning: Morse code is made of dots and long signals

explanation.surface: Hurry off to watch an episode of the detective series Inspector Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to hurry, and the long signal in Morse code is called by the same word.

clue.text: Down to earth, when disgraced

explanation.surface: A person is called sensible at the very moment of their disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen means dropped to the ground, and also having lost one's honour or innocence.

clue.text: Cook's old vessel given a try

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook sailed the ship of this name on his first voyage

explanation.surface: A cook's old pan is given another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is Captain Cook the explorer, not a kitchen cook, and 'vessel' a ship, not a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Endeavour was Captain Cook's ship, and an endeavour is an attempt.

clue.text: Goes out at the front to see part of, roof

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is put out

parts.note: leaves means goes away

explanation.surface: Someone leaves by the front door to inspect a section of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'of' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the lower edges of a roof that overhang the walls.

clue.text: Rules about cheap offers to put up with

indicators.note: the word for rules is turned round

parts.note: laws are rules
low prices are cheap ones

explanation.surface: Regulations govern the bargain deals that shops make.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow an insult is to accept or tolerate it without protest.

clue.text: Notice tenses keep alternating

parts.note: to see is to notice
saw is the past tense of the verb for notice, so the word appears in two tenses

explanation.surface: Someone observes that verb tenses keep switching back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb meaning notice is given in its present and then its past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move repeatedly up and down or back and forth, swinging between states.

clue.text: Essential part of the fare

parts.note: sounds like a bus or train ticket price, but fare here is food on a menu

explanation.surface: A key component of the ticket price for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is a component of a dish, so it is an essential part of food served.

clue.text: Saw deal this way, perhaps, contrary to one's inclination?

definitions.meaning: deal is pine or fir timber, and sawing it across its fibres is one way to cut it
going against one's natural instincts or wishes

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a bargain in a particular way, reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see and 'deal' a bargain; here they are cutting and pine wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting across the fibres of wood goes against the grain, and the idiom means contrary to one's nature.

clue.text: …that can't be ignored — charge at first in supplement

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for supplement

parts.note: an additive is something added as a supplement

indicators.note: only the opening letter of charge is used

explanation.surface: Something compelling carries an initial fee on top of the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive creates a compulsion that is hard to resist or ignore.

clue.text: Tries to sell chap a turtle

parts.note: hawks means peddles goods around
Bill is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A man is trying to sell a turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawksbill is a sea turtle with a hooked beak, prized for tortoiseshell.

clue.text: Sickening, where you have to look for this crossword?

definitions.text: where you have to look for this crossword?
definitions.meaning: in the newspaper this puzzle was printed below the weather forecast

explanation.surface: A tiresome search for where the puzzle sits on the newspaper page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sickening' means falling ill here, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling under the weather is an idiom for being slightly ill.

clue.text: Dazzling tirade? Rising, help to intervene

indicators.note: the turned word comes between letters of the tirade word

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for help reads upwards, so it is backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A speaker's dazzling outburst grows louder and someone steps in to help.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Rising' reads a word upwards; 'to intervene' places it inside the tirade word.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means shining brightly, so it is a synonym of dazzling.

clue.text: Last utensils kept sharp

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words Last utensils

explanation.surface: The last of the kitchen knives were kept keen-edged.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means mentally sharp, shrewd and quick to see an advantage.

clue.text: Turning, spies detectives breaking in, so being scathing?

indicators.note: the detectives go inside the turned letters
the spy agency's letters are turned round

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Spies turn traitor while detectives raid the place, prompting harsh words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses the spy agency's letters, and 'breaking in' puts the detectives after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic remarks are bitingly sharp, so the word fits scathing figuratively.

clue.text: Catch artist looking for source of oil?

parts.note: to cop is to catch
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Police catch an artist searching for a supply of paint oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: I'd followed stray exotic butterfly

indicators.note: the I'd comes after the rearranged letters
exotic suggests something outlandish, so the letters of stray are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone tracked down a rare butterfly that had wandered off.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrids are a family of brown butterflies, the satyrs and browns.

clue.text: One rising ballerina's first to make an entrance in dance

indicators.note: the letter enters the dance word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ballerina is used

explanation.surface: A dancer is the first to come on stage during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One rising' is someone rising up in revolt, not a ballerina lifting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is someone who rises up against authority.

clue.text: Card Frenchman 'held in summit?

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held inside the card word

parts.note: an ace is a playing card
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman holding a card at a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak, a summit.

clue.text: In which tea may be passed round at home

definitions.text: In which tea may be passed round at home

indicators.note: the tea word is put around the home word

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
in means at home

explanation.surface: Fine cups in which tea is handed round at home.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, the cups in which tea is served.

clue.text: Trouble taken with feature-of dining 'room, so it can be decorated

parts.note: pain means trouble or nuisance
a table is the main feature of a dining room

explanation.surface: Trouble is taken with a dining room so it can be redecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen and apostrophe are printing slips.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paintable can be covered in paint, that is decorated.

clue.text: In the end, still, reckon union should be involved

parts.note: even means still, as in even better

indicators.note: the union letter goes inside the reckoning word

parts.note: to tally is to count up or reckon

explanation.surface: Eventually, workers reckon the trade union should get involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means finally, after a long time, so in the end.

clue.text: Boring place to live

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms on one floor, an apartment

explanation.surface: A dull home to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull and lifeless, and is the British word for an apartment.
